output.summary: KEP-2214 proposes adding completion indexes to the Pods of a Job running in fixed completion count mode (an "Indexed Job"), plus stable index-based hostnames so Pods can be addressed via DNS with a headless Service. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
output.rationale: Embarrassingly parallel workloads that need a unique, ordered index per Pod were hard to express with existing Job patterns (external queues or one-Job-per-item templates). Third-party operators worked around this with per-index Services or StatefulSets, which had scalability and serial-creation limits. The KEP adds native indexing to Jobs so each Pod gets an index and a stable hostname derived from it.

alternatives.option: Leave Indexed Job to third-party implementations
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says this splits the ecosystem and leaves Pod management to each implementation, making higher-level Job orchestration harder to support across them.

alternatives.option: Put the completion index in the Pod name (stable Pod names)
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says it would require removing failed Pods before replacement, which is a breaking change and interacts with the tombstone-based backoff tracking; it is deferred as a possible future value for completionMode.

evidence.quote: We propose the addition of completion indexes into the Pods of a *Job [with fixed completion count]* to support running embarrassingly parallel programs
The lack of support for this pattern in k8s forces users to implement their own APIs and controllers or adopt third party implementations.
Each implementation splits the ecosystem, making it harder for higher level systems for Job queueing or workflows to support all of them.
Stable pod names require the Job controller to remove failed Pods before creating a new one with the same index.
However, stable Pod names can be offered later as a new value for `.spec.completionMode` for Jobs.
